chapter_theme: Upasantam (உபசாந்தம்), the stilling: the quiet that comes when the tendencies left by cause and effect fall away, beyond waking and turiya, as the soul is purified, pervaded by the Lord and steeped in Siva's bliss. It ends in union, like water settling clear after waves.
structure_note: 2506 places upasantam among the seeds of release, devotion and attainment; 2507 to 2509 define it through the falling away of maya's effects and causes and the states beyond waking; 2510 and 2511 give its fruit, Siva-bliss, silence and union.

2506.reading: The seed of release is the Lord's own knowledge, the seed of devotion is bowing and clinging to him, the seed of attainment is becoming supreme Siva oneself, and the seed of power is one's own stilling.
2506.nuance: The four lines are built alike on வித்து (seed). சத்தி in the last line can be the Lord's Shakti or simply strength; read either way, upasantam is put last, as the ground of the others' power.

2507.reading: The seven effects hide within maya and the seven causes are hidden in the fierce void; when attachment to the traces left by effect and cause is cut away, that is the nature of upasantam.
2507.nuance: Which seven effects and seven causes are meant is not said; tradition reads them as groups of tattvas. வாதனை (vasana) is the trace or tendency that remains after action. கடுவெளி (the fierce void) and பாரணவும் are obscure.

2508.reading: That turiya is the purifying of the soul; the state beyond waking that it reaches, the lasting vision of the Supreme that comes with it, and upasantam lie in the Lord's pervading of oneself.
2508.nuance: சாக்கிராதீதம் (beyond waking) and ஆத்தும சுத்தி (purifying of the soul) are Siddhanta terms for the higher states. தன்னின் வியாத்தி may be the Lord's pervading of the self or the self's pervading; the syntax is loose.

2509.reading: Removing anava from the states, knowing oneself as the thing to be gained, then complete purity, the unspoken state beyond waking, the guru-Supreme, and the pervasion that is gained: this is upasantam.
2509.nuance: The verse lists stages without connecting words. ஆணவம் is the root mala. ஆறாது அமைந்து (settled, without cooling, or without six) and பிறழ் (flashing, or swerving) in the last line are unclear.

2510.reading: When the traces of upasantam leave the heart, one has become Siva, steeped in Siva's bliss with the joy of silence, and what is settled in it after inquiry is the ten.
2510.nuance: ஈர்ஐந்து (two fives) is taken by tradition as the ten stages of Siddhanta practice (seeing, purifying and knowing the tattvas, the self and Siva), but the verse does not name them. Even the trace of stillness is said to go.

2511.reading: Made one with the Supreme beyond Parai, settled like clear water that had been in waves, he who has known the word and fully tasted the rare nectar has seen the shore, in a reckoning beyond words.
2511.nuance: The water image carries the chapter: waves are the soul's movement, clear water its stilled state, and the water was never other than the sea. பரையின் பரம் is taken as Siva beyond his Shakti. கரைகண்டான் (one who has seen the shore) is the one who has crossed.

links.note: Both speak of a sea to be crossed. The Kural's sea is births, swum only by those at the Lord's feet; Tirumular's knower has already seen the shore, the waves of the soul settled to clear water.

source_issues: 2507 line 4 (பாரண வும்) is obscure and may be corrupt.
